name: Southwest Bend
label: Southwest Bend
about_prose: Southwest Bend sits on the east bank of the Deschutes River, bounded by Powers Road to the north, the river to the west, 3rd Street to the east, and the Bend city limits to the south. The City of Bend formally recognized it on December 5, 2001, the first of what are now 13 neighborhood districts in the city. Like Bend's other districts, it is governed by a volunteer board rather than an HOA. Membership is automatic for any resident or business owner 18 or older inside the boundary, there are no dues, and the group runs on donations. That matters for a buyer: no assessment, no architectural review committee, no design covenant to clear before a remodel.

The district's north edge runs against the Old Mill District, the 270-acre commercial development built on the site of the Shevlin-Hixon and Brooks-Scanlon lumber mills, both established on opposite banks of the river in 1916. At their peak the mills employed more than 2,000 workers apiece. Brooks-Scanlon's Mill B was the last to close, in 1993, the same year William Smith Properties bought the property. The district that opened afterward kept three of the original smokestacks and nine of the mill-era buildings standing. Today it holds 60 stores and restaurants and the 8,000-seat Hayden Homes Amphitheater, built in 2001. For the homes closest to it, that proximity cuts both ways. It's a walk to dinner and a concert most summer weekends, and it's also concert traffic and amplified sound on Old Mill show nights.

The river is the bigger draw for day-to-day living. Riverbend Park, a 13.1-acre city park at 799 SW Columbia St, first acquired in 1999 and developed in 2009, has three improved river-access points and a dog off-leash area, and it connects by trail and footbridge to Farewell Bend Park's boat launch and to the Bend Whitewater Park a short walk north. The whitewater park was built on the site of the removed Colorado Street Dam, funded in part by a 2012 bond measure, and opened in 2015. It carries four named wave features, from Jason's Wave for beginners to Eddy's Wave for advanced paddlers, plus a fish ladder, a series of 12 small rapids near McKay Park, that lets migrating fish move past where the dam used to block them. From Riverbend, the Deschutes River Trail continues south into the South Canyon Reach, about 3 miles of paved, gravel, and natural surface that runs through a basalt rimrock canyon to the Conley Brooks Bridge, with the Old Mill Reach trail looping back on the opposite bank. In July, paddleboards, kayaks, and inner tubes on the river are as much a fixture of the neighborhood as any yard.

SW Century Drive runs through the district and, once it crosses the river heading west, becomes the Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway toward Mount Bachelor, about 22 miles away. On the east side, the boundary runs along 3rd Street, which carries the US 97 Business Route designation left over from before the Bend Parkway took the main highway traffic in 2001, and it sees the commercial traffic that comes with a business route. Elk Meadow Elementary, a Bend-La Pine K-5 school at 60880 Brookswood Blvd ranked in the top 20 percent of Oregon public elementary schools, serves much of the district. Middle and high school assignment is less settled. When Bend-La Pine opened Caldera High School in 2021, it drew new boundaries using SE Reed Market Road, the street Farewell Bend Park sits on, as one dividing line, sending students south of it to the new school while Summit High retained mainly the Century Drive corridor northwest of the river. A specific address inside this district can land on either side of that line, so check it against Bend-La Pine's own attendance-boundary tool before assuming which high school it feeds.

amenities.name: Farewell Bend Park
amenities.description: A 22-acre park at 1000 SW Reed Market Road with a river boat launch, boardwalk, picnic shelters, playground, and a Deschutes River Trail connection.
amenities.access: On foot or bike via the river trail

amenities.name: Bend Whitewater Park
amenities.description: A three-channel whitewater facility on the Deschutes at 166 SW Shevlin Hixon Drive, with four wave features for kayaks, SUP, and surfboards, plus a separate fish-passage channel.

amenities.name: Old Mill District
amenities.description: A 270-acre mixed-use district on the former lumber-mill site, with about 60 stores and restaurants and the Hayden Homes Amphitheater. The three original smokestacks are preserved.
amenities.access: Walking distance from the northern portion via the river trail

amenities.name: Riverbend Park
amenities.description: A river-access park at 799 SW Columbia St for floating, connected to the Whitewater Park, McKay Park, and Farewell Bend Park by trail and footbridge.
amenities.access: On-site parking; Old Mill Reach trailhead

amenities.name: Elk Meadow Elementary
amenities.description: A Bend-La Pine Schools K-5 at 60880 Brookswood Blvd serving much of southwest Bend, ranked in the top 20% of Oregon public elementary schools.
amenities.access: Attendance zone covers most of the district

amenities.name: Deschutes River Trail (Old Mill Reach)
amenities.description: A 2.7-mile paved, level trail along the Deschutes connecting Farewell Bend, Riverbend, McKay, and Miller's Landing, with three footbridges for loops on both banks.
amenities.access: Multiple trailheads within and beside the district

drive_times.note: Walkable from the northern portion; a short drive from the south end
Via SW Century Drive onto the Cascade Lakes Highway (OR-46), about 22 miles
